agents.alertsDescription: Who hears about this agent when nobody is watching it. A run started from chat says what happened on screen; the same run started by a schedule, a channel or the API stops silently, and this is what closes that gap. <link>Your own switches</link> still apply on top and can only ever remove you from a list.
agents.answersCustomerQuestionsFrom: Answers customer questions from the product wiki.
agents.approvalHintDefaultReadOnly: Runs without approval, because this capability only reads.
agents.approvalHintDefaultSideEffecting: Held for approval, because this capability changes something outside the agent.
agents.approvalHintNeverReadOnly: No approval, which is what this capability would do anyway.
agents.approvalHintNeverSideEffecting: The agent acts unattended. Only for actions your organization has decided are safe.
agents.approvalHintRequired: A person approves every call before it runs.
agents.approvalParksTheRun: A tool that asks for approval parks the run until somebody answers in this dashboard, so on a chat platform the thread sits there meanwhile - which reads as the bot being broken. For an agent people reach from a channel, the workable setting is a shell that is not gated, inside a container with no network.
agents.archived: Agent archived. Its history and runs are kept.
agents.audienceAdminsHint: This organization's owners and admins, plus the deployment's app admins.
agents.audienceChosenHint: A standing list, whoever happened to run it.

agents.audienceOwnerHint: The person who would fix this agent's configuration.

agents.backendServiceDetail: Files and a shell, on a sandbox connection your operator registered.
agents.backendStateDetail: Files but no shell, stored here. Works on every deployment.

agents.botTokenHintTelegram: The token @BotFather gives you when you create a bot
agents.capabilityUsesNoSecret: This capability uses no secret, so the one selected for it would be stored and never read. Publishing refuses it.
agents.channelCanOverrideScope: Each channel this agent is published to can override it.
agents.channelLookupsHint: Only what this platform can answer is listed. The agent sees exactly what the bot sees, so it has to be in the channel first.
agents.channelLookupsOn: What this agent may look up on {platform}
agents.channelPromptHint: Added to the agent's instructions here only. A new channel opens with what that client renders and how a link is written there - change it, add to it, or clear it.

agents.collectionScopeHint: The model chooses what to look for; it can never widen where it looks. <link>Manage collections</link>
agents.connectionNoLongerAllows: This connection no longer allows {runtime}. Pick one it does, or the agent fails on its first tool call.
agents.considerOnlyMostLikely: Consider only the most likely tokens making up this much probability mass. Set this or temperature, not both.
agents.costReportingHint: Whether a reply says what the turn cost. It is recorded either way - 'the bot went quiet' is a question somebody asks days later.
agents.createdDraft: Created {name} - a draft, nothing published yet
agents.delegateCount: {count, plural, =0 {nobody to delegate to} =1 {1 subagent} other {# subagents}}
agents.delegateNameClash: Something else here is also called {name}. The model addresses a subagent by name, so one of the two would never be reached.
agents.delegatePinBehind: {by, plural, =1 {One version behind} other {# versions behind}}: pinned at v{version}, and v{latest} is what this delegate publishes now. Nothing changes here until you say so.
agents.delegatePinGoneDetail: This version no longer exists, so a run that reaches this delegate fails and names it. There is deliberately no fall back to the current version.
agents.delegatePinnedTwice: Pinned twice. Two pins of one agent are two delegates answering to one name, so the model cannot say which it meant - and the spec refuses it before it reaches the server.
agents.delegateUnreachableDetail: This organization no longer has it, or you may not see it. Publishing will refuse it either way - remove it, or ask for access to it.
agents.delegatesDetail: Published agents this one may hand work to, each frozen at a version.
agents.delegatingNeedsRunPermission: Delegating needs permission to run agents, which you do not have here. Publishing checks each delegate against the publisher's own access, so this is the same refusal, earlier.
agents.delegationModeAsyncDetail: The parent keeps working and collects the answer later. Worth it for one slow specialist, and a poor default.
agents.delegationModeAutoDetail: The parent's model chooses per call. It has the task in front of it, and nothing else does.
agents.delegationModeFollowDetail: Whatever the policy below says, so changing it moves every delegate that never disagreed.
agents.delegationModeSyncDetail: The parent stops until the delegate answers. The default, and what makes a delegation read like a function call.
agents.delegationOffButConfigured: Delegation is switched off, so none of this is reached. The delegates below stay in the spec and are still checked at publish - switch it on above, or remove them.
agents.delegationPolicyDetail: What bounds every delegation this agent makes, delegates and specialists alike.
agents.delegationPolicyNoSchema: This deployment's delegation capability publishes no configuration schema, so there is nothing to set here. Depth, fan-out and mode arrive with it.
agents.deploymentSOwnShortlist: This deployment's own shortlist - the provider could not be asked. Any id it accepts still works.
agents.draftDiffersHint: The draft is saved. Everything published - channels, widgets, the API - keeps answering with v{version} until you publish.
agents.everyPageCarryingIts: Every page carrying its key stops working immediately. The key cannot be reissued - a new widget gets a new one.
agents.everyRunAlreadyTraced: Every run is already traced into the Logfire project this deployment is configured with. Pick a write token to send this agent's runs to a project of its own instead - an agent built for a client traces into the client's project, with their retention and their alerting.
agents.everyoneWhoTalksAgent: Everyone who talks to this agent reads and writes the same files. A file one person uploads is visible to the rest of the organization. Publishing this is recorded in the audit log.
agents.everythingBelowAppliesAgent: Everything below applies to this agent alone.
agents.filesWorkspaceHasNo: The Files workspace has no shell — pair it with Run Python to compute.
agents.gatewayLitellmProxyModel: A gateway, a LiteLLM proxy, or a model server on this network. Give one and the key becomes optional — there is nothing to authenticate against on your own hardware.
agents.handleDescription: It will be mentioned as <at>{handle}</at>, which is fixed once created and is how Slack and the API address it.
agents.hostOperatorRegisteredCredential: A host an operator registered. The credential lives in the vault, not in this spec.
agents.hostedIntegration: Link - for somebody with no site of their own
agents.hostedLinkProtection: Anyone with the link can talk to this agent. What protects it is that the key cannot be guessed, plus this embed's rate limit, its budget and its pause switch - nothing else.
agents.hostedLogoHint: Whichever you upload elsewhere - there is no second upload here, and no URL for this page to go fetching.
agents.hostedRequiredNotUrlSafe: Required and not URL-safe: {names}. A hosted page can only be told a variable through its own URL, so mark it URL-safe or make it optional.
agents.hostedTitleHint: Shown in the browser tab. Empty uses the agent's name.
agents.hostedWelcomeHint: Shown above the composer before the first question. The agent never sees it, so it is not a turn it thinks it took.
agents.howAgentsReferModel: How agents refer to this model
agents.howLongOneModel: How long one model request may take before it is abandoned.
agents.howVariedAnswerNear: How varied the answer is. Near 0 for classification and extraction, higher for drafting. Some providers cap this at 1, and reasoning models reject it entirely - leave it alone there.
agents.leaveEmptyProviderS: Leave empty for the provider's own API
agents.listedByProviderJust: Listed by the provider just now.
agents.longestAnswerModelMay: The longest answer the model may generate.
agents.mapArchivedDetail: This delegate has been archived since it was pinned, so every run that reaches it is refused. Unarchive it, or repin this agent without it.
agents.mapCycleDetail: Delegation returns to an agent already above it on this branch. A run refuses the loop rather than following it.
agents.mapDepthCapDetail: Has delegates of its own that a run starting from this agent can never reach - the delegation depth cap stops here, or its delegation is switched off.
agents.mapPinBehindDetail: This delegate has published past the pinned version. Nothing changes here until somebody repins it.
agents.mapSpecialistDetail: Defined inside this agent, with no page of its own.
agents.mapTreeLoading: Walking the delegation tree - delegates below the first level are not drawn yet.
agents.mapTreeTruncated: The delegation tree is larger than one response walks, so its deepest parts are not drawn.
agents.mapTreeUnavailable: The full delegation tree could not be loaded, so only direct delegates are shown.
agents.mattermostWebhookTokenHint: The token Mattermost shows for the outgoing webhook
agents.mentionableOnBoundBots: A published agent answers in the dashboard and through the API. To reach it from a chat platform, add the bot here - an agent is mentionable by @handle only on the bots it is bound to.
agents.modelIdOpenRouterHint: Namespaced by origin, as OpenRouter lists it - openai/gpt-5, anthropic/claude-opus-5.
agents.modelIdProviderHint: As the provider names it. Free text, because they ship new ones faster than any list here could be updated.
agents.modelTheseRunsHad: A model in these runs had no price, so this is a floor.
agents.name: Name
agents.namedSoOrganizationCan: Named, so an organization can rotate a key or repoint every agent at once.
agents.nativeClientOriginNote: A browser sends an Origin header for you. A client of your own must set one that is on the allowed-sites list below, or the socket closes with 4003.
agents.noDelegatesYet: No delegates yet. Only a published agent can be one - there is a version to pin.
agents.noMembersChooseFrom: No members to choose from - this organization is just you.
agents.noProviderKeyAddOneHere: No {provider} key in the vault yet. Add one here and it is stored for every agent in this organization.
agents.noProviderKeyAskSomebody: No {provider} key in the vault yet, and storing one needs a permission you do not hold. Somebody who can manage this organization's vault has to add it before this model will run.
agents.noSecretSelected: No secret selected. This capability needs one of kind {kind}, and the agent cannot be published until it has one.
agents.noSitesAllowedWidget: No sites allowed - this widget cannot open anywhere
agents.noSpecialistsYet: No specialists. One is worth adding when publishing a whole agent would be too much ceremony for the job.
agents.noToolsChangesHow: no tools - changes how it runs
agents.nobodySetHearAdd: Nobody is set to hear this. Add an audience, or switch the alert off.
agents.notAvailableAnyChannel: Not available on any channel yet.
agents.notIndexedCount: {count, plural, =1 {1 not indexed} other {# not indexed}}
agents.notPublishedAnySite: Not published to any site yet.
agents.nothingToShareWithDelegates: This agent is bound to nothing else, so there is nothing to pass on.
agents.offRemovesShellEntirely: Off removes the shell entirely, rather than asking before each command.
agents.onePerLineDifferent: One per line. A different port or subdomain is a different site - the browser treats them as such, so this list has to.
agents.optionalPointModelAt: Optional. Point this model at a gateway or proxy instead of the provider's own API; the key is still what authenticates.
agents.organizationAposSOwn: The organization's own monthly cap is not here. It stops every agent in the organization and an agent's author cannot raise it, so its alert always goes to the admins.
agents.organizationHasNoChannel: No bot is free to bind. A bot answers as one agent, so one already serving another agent is not offered here - register another under Channels.
agents.organizationHasNoCollections: This organization has no collections yet. An agent with none searches nothing.
agents.organizationHasNoModels: This organization has no models yet. An agent cannot run without one.
agents.noModelAskAdmin: Models are added in the Builder by a member who manages connections. Once one exists, it can be chosen here.
agents.organizationHasRegisteredNo: This organization has registered no sandbox connection, so this agent cannot be published with a container. An operator adds one under Sandboxes.
agents.organizationHasWrittenNo: This organization has written no skills yet.
agents.orphanedCollections: This agent also references {count, plural, =1 {1 collection} other {# collections}} this organization no longer has. Publishing is refused until they are cleared:
agents.orphanedServers: This agent also references {count, plural, =1 {1 server} other {# servers}} this organization does not offer - removed since, or carried in from an imported spec. Publishing is refused until they are cleared:
agents.orphanedSkills: This agent also references {count, plural, =1 {1 skill} other {# skills}} this organization no longer has. Publishing is refused until they are cleared:
agents.pausedHandleAnswersNothing: Paused - the handle answers nothing here.
agents.promoteSpecialistDetail: Creates a draft agent from this specialist. It is not published, not pinned as a delegate, and this specialist stays where it is.
agents.providerPublishesNoList: This provider publishes no list here. Type the model id as the provider names it.
agents.publishFirstCreatesProduction: The first publish creates the production environment pointing at v{version}, and the agent starts answering with it immediately.
agents.publishFreezesDraft: The draft is frozen as v{version} - a published version never changes.
agents.publishMovesDefault: {name} moves to v{version} the moment you publish.
agents.publishPinnedStays: {name} stays on v{version} - promoting it is a separate step.
agents.readHereFirstSettings: Read it here first - the settings below are what switching it on configures.
agents.runningThemOneAt: Running them one at a time makes a conversation easier to follow, and easier to approve.
agents.runtimesUnreadable: {error} Until it answers, the runtimes it allows cannot be listed here.
agents.scopeAgentDetail: One shared workspace for the whole organization.
agents.scopeChannelDetail: Every thread in one channel shares. Direct messages stay separate.
agents.scopeConversationDetail: Everyone in the chat. On Slack a thread is a chat, so threads do not share.
agents.scopeUserDetail: One workspace per person, across every surface they reach this agent on.
agents.scriptTagIntegration: Script tag - for a site you do not control
agents.secretMissingFromVault: The secret selected here is not in this organization's vault - it was deleted, or the spec was written against another organization. Publishing refuses it.
agents.secretOfWrongKind: "{name}" is of kind {kind}; this capability needs {needed}. Publishing refuses it.
agents.separatesStagingTrafficFrom: Separates staging traffic from the real thing in the same project.
agents.servesVersion: serves v{version}{isDefault, select, true { - what publish repoints} other {}}
agents.shareWithDelegatesDetail: A delegate runs on its own spec. Only what this agent is itself bound to can be shared, so a delegate is never the quiet route to a capability nobody granted.
agents.skillLoadingHint: The agent loads a skill only when it decides one is relevant, so twenty skills cost almost nothing in context. <link>Manage skills</link>
agents.socketIntegration: WebSocket - for an interface you are building
agents.specialistDescriptionDetail: What the parent's model reads when deciding whether to delegate here - the highest-leverage sentence in a delegation. “Researches a topic and cites sources” gets used; “helper” does not.
agents.specialistNameBlank: A specialist the model cannot address is one it cannot use.
agents.specialistNameClash: Something else here is also called {name}, so one of the two would never be reached.
agents.specialistNamePattern: Letters, digits, underscores and dashes only. The model emits this verbatim.
agents.specialistNameTooLong: At most 64 characters - it becomes a tool argument.
agents.specialistsNotVersioned: Defined here, not published: a specialist has no version, cannot be pinned, and changes the moment this agent is edited.
agents.startsAsDraftNothing: It starts as a draft. Nothing runs until you publish it.
agents.storeInVaultHint: <link>Store one in the vault</link> and it appears here - this shape has several fields, so it is filled in there. The value stays in the vault; an agent records which secret to use, never the secret.
agents.storedVaultNeverShown: Stored in the vault and never shown again. Your backend signs each visitor a HS256 token with it.
agents.storedVaultUnderTracing: Stored in the vault under Tracing. The spec keeps the reference, never the token.
agents.toolNameBlank: The model calls the tool by this name, so it cannot be blank.
agents.toolNamePattern: Letters, digits and underscores only - the model calls this name verbatim.
agents.toolNameSteersModel: A tool's name and description are the prompt the model reads before it decides to call it, so both steer it: <mono>{reached}</mono> is reached for on questions <mono>{passed}</mono> is passed over for. Edits here apply to this agent alone.
agents.unchangedLines: {count, plural, =1 {1 unchanged line} other {# unchanged lines}}
agents.urlSafeHint: A hosted page can only be told a variable through its own URL, and a URL is something the visitor types. Mark only what is safe for them to set.
agents.variableDescriptionPlaceholder: Which plan this visitor is on
agents.vaultCouldNotBeRead: The vault could not be read
agents.vaultUnreadableDetail: The vault could not be read, so nothing can be chosen here - which says nothing about what your organization has stored. Listing secrets needs the permission that manages connections. {error}
agents.whatAgentCalledLogfire: What the agent is called in Logfire.
agents.whatServiceAllowsNever: What the service allows. It never names an image — that is the operator's decision.

agents.widgetPublished: Widget published. Copy the snippet into your site.
agents.widgetRemoved: Widget removed. Every page carrying its key has stopped working.
agents.youArePricingPage: You are on the pricing page. Answer in German.
agents.youNotVisitorsWhich: For you, not for visitors - which placement this is.
agents.yourBackendSignsToken: Your backend signs a token we verify
agents.publicSurfacesDescription: A published agent already answers in this dashboard and through the API. These are the surfaces you open to the public - each one runs the same frozen version, under the same budget and the same approval gate.
agents.surfaceWidgetBody: A chat bubble on a site you do not control. One script tag, no build step. The list of allowed sites is what protects it, because the key in the tag is public.
agents.surfacePageBody: A link we serve, at /e/ plus the key. No site of your own and nothing to paste - what protects it is the key being unguessable, plus the rate limit and the budget.
agents.surfaceSocketBody: The protocol the widget speaks, for an interface you build yourself: a mobile app, a kiosk, a component in your own design system.
agents.surfaceApiBody: Run the agent from your own backend with an organization API key. Nothing to publish here.
agents.surfaceApiNotes: The API needs a credential your organization already has, and no per-agent setup, so there is nothing on this screen to configure. Whoever holds the key runs the agent as the caller it belongs to.
agents.surfaceDashboardAlways: Any member who can see this agent can already chat with it in the dashboard. That needs nothing here.
agents.originsSocketHint: A browser sends Origin for you; a client of your own sends nothing unless you set it, and an unset one is refused with close code 4003.
agents.secretUnchanged: Leave blank to keep the stored secret
agents.hostedLogoLimits: PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, up to 2MB.
agents.hostedLogoPublishFirst: Publish the page first - an upload needs somewhere to go. The picture can be added the moment it exists.
agents.pageAllowVoiceHint: Dictation using the visitor's own browser. No audio reaches this deployment and nothing is transcribed here - but a browser that offers it hands the audio to its vendor, so this is off unless you turn it on.
agents.pageAllowNewConversation: A button to start a fresh thread
agents.pageAllowNewConversationHint: The old thread is not deleted. It stops being the one this browser resumes.
agents.widgetGreetingHint: Drawn by the widget before anybody types. It is never sent to the model - a greeting in the model's history is a turn the agent thinks it took.
agents.pageAllowFiles: A way to attach a file
agents.pageAllowFilesHint: The only thing here that lets a stranger store something on this deployment. The file goes through the same checks and parser a member's upload does, under a smaller cap and a limit per visitor - and the agent reads it the way it reads any attachment.
agents.pageShows: What the visitor sees of the work
agents.pageShowsHint: These decide what the server sends, not what the page draws. A visitor who opens devtools sees exactly what is ticked here and nothing else.
agents.pageShowToolStepsHint: One line per step - Searching the documents, Running a query. On, because a page that goes quiet for thirty seconds reads as broken.
agents.pageShowToolResultsHint: The arguments a step was called with and what came back. Written for the model, so this is where something internal turns up - an address, a row from a system, a passage nobody meant to publish.
agents.pageShowThinkingHint: What the model says to itself before it answers. It is not written for anybody to read and it is not an answer you can stand behind.

kb.appliesEachFileYou: This applies to each file you add next and is recorded on it. The collection keeps its own settings - every later upload goes back to them.
kb.builtInReadersRegardless: Text, Markdown and Word files use the built-in readers whichever is chosen.
kb.charactersEachPieceRepeats: Characters each piece repeats from the one before it, so a sentence split across a boundary is still findable.
kb.charactersPerEmbeddedPiece: Characters per embedded piece. Smaller pieces match a question more precisely; larger ones carry more of the surrounding argument.
kb.chunkingFixedHint: A fixed number of characters, structure ignored.
kb.chunkingMarkdownHint: Split on headings, so a chunk stays inside one section.
kb.chunkingRecursiveHint: Split on paragraphs, then sentences, then words - whatever fits.
kb.chunkingSummary: {size, plural, =1 {1 character} other {# characters}}, {overlap, number} overlapping · {strategy}
kb.configuredOnceUsedAs: Configured once, used in as many knowledge bases as you like. Each copy syncs on its own schedule.
kb.describedByModelIndexed: Described by a model and indexed
kb.everyPageCameBack: Every page came back as empty scaffolding, which is what an unreadable scan looks like. If this file is a scan or a photo, turn on reading scanned pages in the parse options and upload it again.
kb.formatMarkdownHint: Rebuilds headings, tables and lists - what the Markdown chunking strategy splits on.
kb.formatTextHint: Keeps the page's spatial grid, so a table stays aligned but carries no structure.
kb.frozenAtCreationCollection: Frozen at creation: the collection's vectors are produced by this model and cannot be re-indexed under another one later. The key decides whose account pays for embedding.
kb.howFinelyPageRendered: How finely a page is rendered before OCR reads it. Higher recovers faint scans and costs time.
kb.howHardModelThinks: How hard the model thinks before describing an image. A level a provider does not have maps to its closest one.
kb.howLongLiteparseMay: How long LiteParse may spend on one document before it is abandoned.
kb.howVariedEachDescription: How varied each description is. Left alone the parameter is not sent at all, which is not the same as sending zero - reasoning models reject it outright.
kb.ingestionRecordedNote: What this collection was indexed with, recorded when it was created. It cannot be changed - vectors written by two different models are not comparable, so a collection that needs another one is a new collection.
kb.ingestionSettingsDescription: How documents added to <mono>{name}</mono> are read from here on. Nothing already indexed is re-parsed.
kb.integrationSaved: Integration saved - use it in a knowledge base to start syncing
kb.itsCredentialsAreCopied: Its credentials are copied into an independent source. The original stays here for the next knowledge base that needs it.
kb.keyHereBillsEmbeddings: A key here bills embeddings to this organization instead of using the deployment's.
kb.knowledgeBasesAlreadyUsing: Knowledge bases already using it keep their own copy - this only removes the one nothing is syncing from.
kb.leftAloneCollectionInherits: Left alone, this collection inherits whatever defaults the deployment is configured with. The values below are the platform's; changing any one of them sends all of them, and they become this collection's until somebody edits them.
kb.liteparseReadsTextLayer: LiteParse reads the text layer first and OCRs a page only when there is nothing there. OCR dominates the cost of a parse, and most documents are born digital. Turn this off to OCR every page regardless.
kb.modelsUnreadable: The list of models could not be read. This collection will be created on the deployment's default.
kb.name: Name
kb.notDescribedPictureTable: Not described - a picture of a table is not searchable
kb.nothingHereYetAdd: Nothing here yet. Add one to connect a source before you know which knowledge bases will need it.
kb.nothingIndexedDocumentIts: Nothing is indexed for this document. Its vectors may have been removed since it was ingested.
kb.nothingReadableCameOut: Nothing readable came out of this parse
kb.ocrLanguageHint: Tesseract codes, which are three letters: “eng”, “pol”, “deu”. Join several with “+”.
kb.onlyOcrPagesNeed: Only OCR the pages that need it
kb.overlapRepeats: adjacent chunks repeat their overlap, so boundary text appears twice
kb.pageParsedNothingReadable: This page parsed to nothing readable - likely an unreadable scan.
kb.pagePictureTextCarries: A page that is a picture of text carries no text to extract. PyMuPDF hands such a page to the image model; LiteParse runs its own OCR.
kb.parserLiteparseHint: Local, with its own OCR. Also reads spreadsheets, slide decks and images.
kb.parserLlamaparseHint: A hosted service that reconstructs layout, tables and columns. Billed per page.
kb.parserPymupdfHint: Local and fast. Reads the text a PDF already carries.
kb.problemOcrLanguage: Tesseract codes are three letters - "eng", not "en". Join several with "+", as in "eng+pol".
kb.problemOverlapTooLarge: Must be smaller than the chunk size of {size}.
kb.problemTimeoutRange: More than 0 and at most {max} seconds.
kb.sendPicturesInsideDocument: Send the pictures inside a document to a model and index what it says about them. Needs a model profile with a working key, which is checked when this is saved.
kb.tierAgenticHint: Reads structure the way a person would.
kb.tierAgenticPlusHint: The most thorough, and the dearest.
kb.tierFastHint: Cheapest, and the least faithful to layout.
kb.whatDocumentsWillKb: What documents will this KB contain?
kb.whatModelAskedSay: What the model is asked to say about each image. What it answers is what a search matches, so name the things worth finding.
kb.whatWasIndexed: What was indexed: {count, plural, =1 {1 chunk} other {# chunks}}
kb.whereLiteparseStopsWhat: Where LiteParse stops. This is what bounds the cost of one document - the timeout only bounds the wait.
kb.whoseAccountEachParse: Whose account each parse is billed to.

pl.jeLiKorzystaszZ: Jeśli korzystasz z Usługi w imieniu organizacji, akceptujesz Regulamin w jej imieniu i potwierdzasz, że masz do tego upoważnienie.
pl.jeLiWymagaTego: jeśli wymaga tego prawo, ale walczymy gdzie możemy i powiadamiamy dotkniętych użytkowników gdzie jest to prawnie dozwolone.
pl.jesteWCicielemTego: Jesteś właścicielem tego, co wprowadzasz - promptów, dokumentów, treści rozmów („Dane Klienta”). Udzielasz nam ograniczonej licencji na hostowanie, przetwarzanie i wyświetlanie Danych Klienta wyłącznie w celu obsługi Usługi dla Ciebie.
pl.kredytyWygasajNaKo: Kredyty wygasają na końcu każdego cyklu rozliczeniowego. Top-upy pay-as-you-go nie wygasają. Podatki są naliczane gdzie ma to zastosowanie.
pl.maYPlikKt: Mały plik, który Twoja przeglądarka przechowuje na urządzeniu gdy odwiedzasz stronę. Cookies pozwalają nam utrzymywać Cię zalogowanego, pamiętać preferencje i rozumieć jak używane są funkcje.

Sekcje, które powinny przetrwać wypowiedzenie (IP, wyłączenia odpowiedzialności, ograniczenia odpowiedzialności, rozstrzyganie sporów) przetrwają.

pl.pamiTajTwojeWybory: Pamiętają Twoje wybory by Usługa nie była powtarzalna. Opcjonalne.

pl.usUgaNieJest: Usługa nie jest skierowana do dzieci poniżej 16 roku życia. Świadomie nie zbieramy od nich informacji.
pl.usUgaPolegaNa: Usługa polega na dostawcach zewnętrznych (np. API modeli, procesorzy płatności). Korzystanie z tych funkcji podlega też regulaminom tych dostawców. Nie kontrolujemy ich i nie odpowiadamy za ich działania.
pl.wPrzypadkuFuzjiLub: w przypadku fuzji lub sprzedaży, z zachowaniem zobowiązań tej Polityki.
pl.wZakresieDozwolonymPrawem: W zakresie dozwolonym prawem nasza łączna odpowiedzialność za jakiekolwiek roszczenie wynikające lub związane z Usługą nie przekroczy większej z (a) kwoty, którą nam zapłaciłeś w ciągu 12 miesięcy przed roszczeniem lub (b) 100 USD. Żadna ze stron nie odpowiada za szkody pośrednie, przypadkowe, wynikowe lub karne.
pl.wymaganeDoDziaAnia: Wymagane do działania Usługi. Nie można ich wyłączyć. Przykłady: token sesji, token CSRF, preferowany motyw.
pl.yourRightsDescription: W zależności od miejsca zamieszkania, możesz mieć prawo do dostępu, sprostowania, usunięcia lub eksportu swoich danych osobowych, a także do sprzeciwu lub ograniczenia określonego przetwarzania. Napisz na <mail>privacy@example.com</mail> by je zrealizować. Odpowiadamy w ciągu 30 dni.
pl.zachowujemyWszystkiePrawaDo: Zachowujemy wszystkie prawa do Usługi, w tym oprogramowania, designu i znaków towarowych. Ty zachowujesz wszystkie prawa do swoich Danych Klienta i do output'u, który generujesz za pomocą Usługi, z zastrzeżeniem regulaminów dostawców modeli.
pl.zakCaKorzystaniaZ: zakłócać korzystania z Usługi przez innych klientów.

create-agent.title: Create your first agent?
create-agent.body: An agent is instructions, a model and a set of tools. Want to build your first one together? We'll check what your organization already has and only stop where you need to.

create-skill.title: Create a skill?
create-skill.body: Skills are reusable instructions you can attach to any agent. Want to make your first one now? We'll walk you through it.

create-kb.title: Create a knowledge base?
create-kb.body: A knowledge base lets your agents search your documents. Want to set one up now? We'll walk you through it.

create-mcp.title: Connect an MCP server?
create-mcp.body: MCP servers give agents tools from other systems. Want to add a connection now? We'll walk you through it.

create-org.title: Create an organization?
create-org.body: An organization is a separate space with its own agents, members and settings. Want to create one now? We'll walk you through it.

explore-chat.title: Take a quick tour of chat?
explore-chat.body: See how to start a conversation, switch which agent answers, and change the model or thinking effort for a single chat. Want a quick guided run through it?

flow-agent-create.title: Name your agent
flow-agent-create.body: Choose New agent, give it a name and a short description, and create it. That opens the builder, where the rest of this happens. We'll move on as soon as it's created.

flow-agent-instructions.title: Write its instructions
flow-agent-instructions.body: Tell the agent who it is and what it should do — this is its system prompt. Write a line or two, then choose Next.

flow-agent-model-add.title: Add a model
flow-agent-model-add.body: Your organization has no model yet. Pick a provider, name a model, and paste a key — it's stored in the vault and the model is ready. We'll move on once it's added.

flow-agent-model-pick.title: Choose its model
flow-agent-model-pick.body: Pick the model this agent should run on from the list — an agent needs one to run, so we'll move on once it's set.

flow-agent-model-none.title: No model in this organization yet
flow-agent-model-none.body: An agent needs a model to run, and this organization has none. Adding one needs the connections permission you don't have — ask an admin to add a model, then this agent can use it. Choose Next to look at the rest for now.

flow-agent-knowledge.title: Give it documents to read (optional)
flow-agent-knowledge.body: Attach a knowledge base and the agent can search those documents and cite them. You can skip this and add one anytime — choose Next to move on.

flow-agent-knowledge-ask.title: No knowledge base yet — create one?
flow-agent-knowledge-ask.body: A knowledge base lets this agent search your documents and cite them, and you don't have one yet. Want to create one now and attach it? We'll guide you there and all the way back.

flow-agent-knowledge-create.title: Create the knowledge base
flow-agent-knowledge-create.body: Choose New knowledge base — the form opens and we'll walk it together, field by field. Afterwards we'll walk you back to your agent.

flow-agent-knowledge-return-nav.title: Back to your agents
flow-agent-knowledge-return-nav.body: Choose Agents in the sidebar to head back to the agent you were building.

flow-agent-knowledge-return-edit.title: Open your agent again
flow-agent-knowledge-return-edit.body: Choose the edit pencil on the agent you just built to reopen its builder.

flow-agent-knowledge-attach.title: Attach what you made
flow-agent-knowledge-attach.body: Open the Knowledge tab and attach the knowledge base you just created, then choose Next.

flow-agent-skills.title: Give it skills (optional)
flow-agent-skills.body: A skill is written know-how the agent loads when it's relevant — a refund policy, a house style. Attach any, or choose Next to move on.

flow-agent-skills-ask.title: No skills yet — create one?
flow-agent-skills-ask.body: A skill is written know-how the agent loads when it's relevant, and you don't have one yet. Want to create one now and attach it? We'll guide you there and all the way back.

flow-agent-skills-create.title: Create the skill
flow-agent-skills-create.body: Choose New skill — the form opens and we'll walk it together, field by field. Afterwards we'll walk you back to your agent.

flow-agent-skills-return-nav.title: Back to your agents
flow-agent-skills-return-nav.body: Choose Agents in the sidebar to head back to the agent you were building.

flow-agent-skills-return-edit.title: Open your agent again
flow-agent-skills-return-edit.body: Choose the edit pencil on the agent you just built to reopen its builder.

flow-agent-skills-attach.title: Attach your skill
flow-agent-skills-attach.body: Open the Skills tab and attach the skill you just created, then choose Next.

flow-agent-tools.title: Give it tools (optional)
flow-agent-tools.body: Capabilities let the agent do things — search the web, run code, call another system. Switch on what it needs, or choose Next to move on.

flow-agent-mcp.title: Add MCP servers (optional)
flow-agent-mcp.body: MCP servers give the agent tools from other systems you've connected. Attach any here, or choose Next to move on.

flow-agent-mcp-ask.title: No MCP server connected — connect one?
flow-agent-mcp-ask.body: An MCP server gives this agent tools from another system, and you haven't connected one yet. Want to connect one now? It's a quick dialog right here — no leaving the builder, and we'll pick up the moment it's connected.

flow-agent-mcp-connect.title: Open the catalog
flow-agent-mcp-connect.body: Choose Connect a server — the catalog opens right here in the builder, and we'll pick one together.

flow-agent-limits.title: Set a budget (optional)
flow-agent-limits.body: Cap what this agent can spend in a month and how many steps one run may take, and choose who's told when it reaches a limit. It's how an agent that loops or runs away stops itself. Choose Next to move on.

flow-agent-publish.title: Publish it
flow-agent-publish.body: An agent has to be published before you can chat with it — a draft can't take messages. Click Publish to make this version live; we'll move on the moment it's published.

flow-agent-run-pick.title: Pick your agent
flow-agent-run-pick.body: You're in the chat now. Open the picker and choose the agent you just published, so your first message goes to it.

flow-agent-run-send.title: Send it a message
flow-agent-run-send.body: Type a prompt and send it — your agent's first run, and the end of the tour. We'll close the moment it's on its way.

flow-skill-create.title: Add your skill
flow-skill-create.body: Choose New skill — the form opens and we'll walk it together, field by field.

flow-kb-create.title: Create the knowledge base
flow-kb-create.body: Choose New knowledge base — the form opens and we'll walk it together, field by field.

flow-skill-field-name.title: Name it
flow-skill-field-name.body: Short and specific, like refund-policy — it's how the model refers to this skill, and it can't be changed later. Then choose Next.

flow-skill-field-description.title: Say when it applies
flow-skill-field-description.body: This is the only part the model reads when deciding whether to open the skill at all — write when to reach for it, not what's inside. Then choose Next.

flow-skill-field-source.title: Write the skill
flow-skill-field-source.body: Switch to Source and write the know-how itself in Markdown — the steps, the rules, the exceptions. You can refine it anytime after. Then choose Next.

flow-skill-field-create.title: Create it
flow-skill-field-create.body: Choose Create. We'll move on the moment it's saved.

flow-kb-field-name.title: Name it
flow-kb-field-name.body: Name it after what it will hold — Product docs, Support wiki — so anyone attaching it to an agent knows what they're giving it. Then choose Next.

flow-kb-field-scope.title: Choose who it belongs to
flow-kb-field-scope.body: Personal is yours alone; Organization makes it available to every member and agent. For a base your agents will search, pick Organization. Then choose Next.

flow-kb-field-embeddings.title: Embeddings (leave the default)
flow-kb-field-embeddings.body: How documents are indexed for search. It's frozen at creation, but the deployment default is right for almost everyone — expand it only if you know you need a different model. Choose Next.

flow-kb-field-create.title: Create it
flow-kb-field-create.body: Choose Create. We'll move on the moment it exists — you'll add documents to it right after.

flow-mcp-field-pick.title: Pick a server
flow-mcp-field-pick.body: This is the catalog of systems your agents can get tools from. Find the one you want and choose Connect on it.

flow-mcp-field-form.title: Fill in the connection
flow-mcp-field-form.body: Name it — the name prefixes its tool names — keep Organization so your agents can use it, and paste a token if this server asks for one. Then choose Next.

flow-mcp-field-connect.title: Connect it
flow-mcp-field-connect.body: Choose Connect. We check the server answers and move on the moment it's connected — a server that signs in through the provider will hand off to their consent screen instead.

flow-org-create.title: Create the organization
flow-org-create.body: Choose New organization, give it a name, and create it. We'll move on as soon as it exists.

flow-chat-needs-agent.title: No published agent to chat with yet
flow-chat-needs-agent.body: Chat talks to a published agent, and you don't have one yet. Want to build one first? We'll guide you through it and you can come back to chat after. Or skip to look around chat for now.

flow-chat-start.title: Start a conversation
flow-chat-start.body: Choose New conversation to begin a fresh thread. Each one keeps its own history and settings. Choose Next when you've had a look.

flow-chat-agent.title: Choose who answers
flow-chat-agent.body: This picks which of your published agents replies. Open it to switch agents — you can even change partway through a conversation. Choose Next.

flow-chat-controls.title: Tune this conversation
flow-chat-controls.body: Open Controls to run this chat on a different model, or change how hard it thinks — just for this conversation, without touching the agent itself. Choose Next.

flow-chat-composer.title: Type and send
flow-chat-composer.body: Write your message here and send it — that's your first conversation. Choose Finish when you're ready.

welcome.title: Welcome to AgenticOS
welcome.body: This is where your team builds, runs and governs its AI agents. We'll step through each section and point out what's worth noticing — about a minute, and you can close it whenever you like.

dashboard-actions.title: Start here
dashboard-actions.body: These shortcuts are the quickest way in: open a chat, create your first agent, review anything waiting on a decision, or invite a teammate.

dashboard-filters.title: Slice the dashboard
dashboard-filters.body: Every number on this page follows the period you pick here, and you can hide sections you don't need. The view lives in the URL, so it survives a reload and travels in a link.

dashboard-customize.title: Make it your own
dashboard-customize.body: Customize opens an editor where you add, hide and rearrange the cards; Layouts saves an arrangement and switches between them. The dashboard is yours to shape, per person.

chat-start.title: Chat with your agents
chat-start.body: New chat opens a fresh thread, and your past conversations stack up in this rail. It's the quickest way to try an agent out and watch how it works, step by step.

chat-agent-picker.title: Choose who answers
chat-agent-picker.body: Switch between your agents right here. Each brings its own instructions, tools and knowledge, so the same question can get a very different answer.

chat-composer.title: Ask anything
chat-composer.body: Type a message, drop in a file, or start with a slash-command. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line.

chat-model-picker.title: Tune the model
chat-model-picker.body: Pick the model behind the agent and dial its thinking effort or temperature — just for this conversation.

agents-new.title: Build an agent
agents-new.body: An agent is its instructions, a model, and the tools, MCP servers and skills you give it. Create one here, then publish a version so it runs the same way everywhere — chat, API, Slack or a widget.

agents-filters.title: Find one fast
agents-filters.body: Filter by status or search by name once the roster grows past a screenful.

agent-instructions.title: Instructions are the behaviour
agent-instructions.body: Open an agent and you land in the Builder, where it's assembled tab by tab. Build comes first: the instructions are its behaviour, written in plain Markdown rather than code.

agent-model.title: Choose the brain
agent-model.body: The model underneath does the reasoning. Swap it, dial how hard it thinks, or turn on step-by-step reasoning — all without touching the instructions above.

agent-toolbox.title: Give it tools
agent-toolbox.body: The Toolbox is what an agent can actually do. Switch on built-in capabilities like web search, code or files, and each becomes a tool the model may call mid-answer.

agent-mcp.title: And whole tool sets
agent-mcp.body: Below the capabilities, attach MCP servers — ready-made tool sets like GitHub or Slack, connected once for the organization and reused across agents.

agent-knowledge.title: Point it at your docs
agent-knowledge.body: Knowledge lets the agent search the collections you pick, so it answers from your own material instead of guessing from training alone.

agent-skills.title: Hand it a playbook
agent-skills.body: Skills are written know-how the agent reads before it acts — a procedure, a house style, a checklist — and the same one can be shared across agents.

agent-limits.title: Keep it in bounds
agent-limits.body: Cap the monthly spend and the steps a single run may take, and choose who gets told when the agent hits a limit or fails.

agent-availability.title: Put it to work
agent-availability.body: Availability is where a published agent goes live — a web chat, an embed on your site, Slack or Telegram — and where you decide who to share it with.

agent-history.title: Every version, kept
agent-history.body: Each publish freezes the spec as a version you can promote to an environment, roll back to, or read the run history against.

agent-publish.title: Publish to ship it
agent-publish.body: Nothing runs until you publish. Publishing freezes the current draft as a version, and that version is what answers everywhere the agent is available.

skills-new.title: Reusable skills
skills-new.body: A skill is a packaged set of instructions an agent can draw on for a task. Write one once here and share it across the agents that need it.

skills-list.title: Your skills
skills-list.body: The skills you've written or installed. An agent picks the ones it needs from its Skills tab, and the same skill can serve several agents at once.

context-new.title: Add standing context
context-new.body: Context files are the background every agent carries — company facts, tone, terms — injected into each prompt without you pasting them in every time. Add one here.

context-list.title: Shared context
context-list.body: The context files this organization holds. One file can feed every agent, so a fact you fix here is fixed for all of them at once.

channels-new.title: Reach agents where people are
channels-new.body: Register a chat platform — Slack, Telegram, Mattermost — and any agent can be bound to answer there. The bot's token is sealed in the vault. Add one here.

channels-list.title: Connected channels
channels-list.body: The platforms this organization is reachable on. A channel belongs to the organization, not one agent, so the same bot can serve every agent bound to it.

activity-overview.title: Watch activity
activity-overview.body: Every run is recorded with its cost and outcome, so you can see what your agents did and step in when one is waiting on a decision. These figures summarise the lot.

activity-approvals.title: What's waiting on you
activity-approvals.body: Runs that paused for a human decision queue here. Approve or reject each one and the run picks up from where it stopped — this tab only appears if you're allowed to decide them.

activity-runs.title: Every run
activity-runs.body: The full history: who ran which agent, what it cost and how it ended. Filter it, or open a run to see the whole conversation and the tools it called.

activity-spend.title: Where the money went
activity-spend.body: Spend over time and by agent, against the budgets you've set — so an agent quietly getting expensive shows up here before the bill does.

knowledge-new.title: Knowledge bases
knowledge-new.body: Upload documents so your agents can answer from them. Each collection is searchable and stays private to your organization — create your first one here.

knowledge-tabs.title: Browse or search
knowledge-tabs.body: Two views of the same knowledge: the collections you've built, and a search that runs across all of them at once.

knowledge-integrations.title: Reusable connections
knowledge-integrations.body: Connections shared across the organization: set up an S3 bucket, a drive, a site or a repo once here, and clone it into any collection instead of re-configuring it each time.

knowledge-add-integration.title: Add a connection
knowledge-add-integration.body: Start a new one here — pick a connector like S3 or Google Drive, give it credentials, and it becomes available to clone into any collection that needs it.

kb-header.title: Inside a collection
kb-header.body: The collection's name, scope and controls sit up top — refresh it, drop in files, change how they're read, or remove it.

kb-documents.title: What's in it
kb-documents.body: Every document the collection holds, with the status of each as it's parsed and indexed. Add more here, or preview and remove what's already there.

kb-ingestion.title: How documents are read
kb-ingestion.body: The parser, chunking and embedding model behind this collection — what turns your files into something searchable. Change it, and new uploads follow the new settings.

kb-sync.title: Keep it in step
kb-sync.body: Connect a drive, a site or a repo, and the collection refreshes itself from the source instead of waiting on a manual re-upload.

orgs-new.title: Your organizations
orgs-new.body: Everything is scoped to an organization. Create one, or switch between the ones you belong to — each keeps its own agents, keys and knowledge apart.

org-profile.title: Name and face
org-profile.body: The organization's name and avatar, shown wherever it appears. Owners and admins can change them here.

org-members.title: Who's in it
org-members.body: Everyone in the organization and the role each holds. Invite teammates, change a role, or remove someone — all from this list.

org-roles.title: What each role may do
org-roles.body: The permission matrix, role by role: what each may touch and how far it reaches. Sharing a single resource can widen access beyond the role, never narrow it.

vault-new.title: The vault
vault-new.body: API keys and other credentials live here, encrypted at rest. Agents use them to reach the tools they need, and nobody sees a stored secret again.

vault-keys.title: What's stored

agents.agentAposSBehaviour: The agent's behaviour lives here, not in code. Be specific about what it should do, what it should refuse, and how it should cite. Markdown, and the model reads the structure - headings and lists are what make a long prompt followable, so being able to see them rendered is the point of the preview.

agents.connectServerOrganizationBecomes: Connect a server for the organization and it becomes bindable here. A personal connection is for your own chat and is refused at publish, so an agent everyone runs never depends on whose credential is behind it.
agents.createOneGiveInstructions: Create one, give it instructions and a few capabilities, then publish it.
agents.draftAsStandsWhat: The draft as it stands: what reaches this agent, and what it reaches for. A dashed box is something nothing is attached to.
agents.eachPublishFreezesSpec: Each publish freezes a spec. Runs record the version, so what an agent did last Tuesday stays answerable after a dozen edits. Restoring publishes a new version copied from the old one - the timeline shows that a rollback happened rather than pretending the bad version never existed.
agents.howAgentAsksIts: How this agent asks its model to behave, on top of whatever the model profile already sets. A setting nobody touches is not sent at all - that is deliberate rather than tidy: reasoning models reject a temperature outright, so an agent that never chose one must not have one sent on its behalf. A provider that does not implement a setting ignores it. Reasoning itself is a capability, below.
agents.howManyModelRequests: How many model requests one run may make. A tool loop hits this long before it costs enough to hit a budget.
agents.mcpServersDescription: External tools this agent may call, from the servers <servers>your organization has connected</servers>. Only the organization's servers appear here - an agent everyone runs cannot depend on whose credential is behind it, so a personal connection is refused at publish.

agents.removesAgentEveryVersion: This removes the agent, every version of it and every share pointing at it. Its past runs are kept for the record. Archive instead if you only want it to stop.
agents.removesAgentEveryVersion2: This removes the agent, every version of it and every share pointing at it. Its past runs are kept for the record. Archive instead if you only want it to stop.
agents.spendsWithoutCeilingIts: Spends without a ceiling of its own

agents.stopsAnsweringEverywhereAvailable: It stops answering everywhere it is available. Its versions, runs and history are kept, and it can be restored.
agents.stopsAnsweringEverywhereAvailable2: It stops answering everywhere it is available. Its versions, runs and history are kept, and it can be restored.
agents.twoLimitsWorthKnowing: Two limits worth knowing before you rely on this. Which of a server's tools are exposed is set on the connection, so every agent bound to it gets the same ones - not the per-agent choice the capabilities above offer. And MCP tools are outside the approval gate entirely: an approval set on a capability does not cover them, so anything these servers can do, this agent can do without asking.
agents.whatAgentCanDo: What this agent can do, and where it keeps what it produces. Anything that acts on the outside world needs a human approval before it runs.
agents.whatAgentMaySearch: What this agent may search. The model chooses what to look for; it can never widen where it looks. Each collection says what it holds, because attaching an empty one produces an agent that searches, finds nothing, and reads as broken.
agents.whetherAgentWorkingWhat: Whether this agent is working, and what it has cost. The full history - surfaces, tokens, the version each run executed - lives in Activity rather than being half-rebuilt here.
agents.writtenKnowHowAgent: Written know-how the agent loads only when it decides a skill is relevant, so twenty skills cost almost nothing in context. Picking one gives the agent the tools to read them - that used to be a separate capability somebody had to know to switch on, and skills chosen without it were resolved and then dropped on the floor.

sandboxes.readFromServiceItself: Read from the service itself, and only changeable there. These are the ceilings in force for every agent on this connection.

runtime.imageAliasAgentGets: The image alias an agent gets when its own spec names none. Leave empty to take whatever the service defaults to.
runtime.label: Default runtime
runtime.selectedNotOnThisHost: This host did not name the runtime selected. Pick one it did, or an agent taking this default fails on its first tool call.
runtime.shipped: These are the runtimes the sandbox library ships. Test the connection to see which ones this host allows.

sandboxes.serviceAllowsNoRuntime: This service allows no runtime, so no sandbox can start on it. Its allowlist is empty.
sandboxes.serviceSilent: The sandbox service did not answer

sessions.noContainerConnectionHint: What is running can only be listed from a container service. Register one under Connections; Daytona sandboxes are managed on the Daytona account they bill to.
sessions.nothingRunningSandboxOpens: Nothing running. A sandbox opens on an agent's first file or shell call, so an agent that has one and never uses it costs nothing here.

sharing.collectionRuntimeNote: Sharing controls who can pick this collection in the Builder and who can change it. An agent connected to it searches it for everyone who can run that agent, including people who cannot open the collection themselves.
sharing.peopleReaches: A share lifts one person's access to this {resource, select, agent {agent} skill {skill} collection {collection} other {secret}} without changing their role anywhere else. Can view sees the configuration, can use also runs it, can edit also changes it.
sharing.secretRuntimeNote: Sharing controls who can bind this key to an agent and who can rotate it - not who benefits from it. Once an agent uses this key, it runs with it for everyone who can run that agent, including people who cannot see the key here.
sharing.visibilityOrgReaches: Everyone in the organization who can view {resource, select, agent {agents} skill {skills} collection {collections} other {secrets}} at all.
sharing.visibilityPrivateReaches: Only you and the people listed below. Nobody else finds this {resource, select, agent {agent} skill {skill} collection {collection} other {secret}} in their list - and if it has no owner yet, it becomes yours.
sharing.visibilityReaches: Who reaches this {resource, select, agent {agent} skill {skill} collection {collection} other {secret}} without being named. Sharing adds people on top of this; it never takes access away.
sharing.visibilityTeamReaches: Anyone whose role reaches team {resource, select, agent {agents} skill {skills} collection {collections} other {secrets}}. This organization has no teams - pick one of the two above.
